title: Filling a prime grid that holds the prime nineteen
description: A three by three grid has row products sixty three, twenty seven and one hundred and ninety, and column products forty five, forty two and one hundred and seventy one. The video fills the nine cells, and Keeko's doubt that nineteen is too big to be a prime is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a big product such as one hundred and ninety needs a big prime, and the divisors of the number, not its size, decide whether it is a prime. Watch for students who think a prime in the grid must be a single digit.

source: Fill the 3 by 3 grid with prime numbers only so that the product of each row is the number to the right of the row and the product of each column is the number below the column. Row products: 63, 27, 190. Column products: 45, 42, 171.
video_script.why: The child fills the row that has only one choice, then uses the primes each row and column allows to place the five, the nineteen, the two and the seven.
video_script.substitution: Fill the row made of one prime, then place each remaining prime where the row and the column both allow it.
video_script.anchor: an empty 3 by 3 grid with 63, 27 and 190 at the right of the rows and 45, 42 and 171 below the columns
video_script.wrong_answer: nineteen is too big to be a prime
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says nineteen is too big to be a prime. Two, three, four, five and every number up to eighteen leave something over, so only one and nineteen divide it, and the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: The rows are three, seven, three, then three, three, three, then five, two, nineteen

final_answer.spoken: the rows are three, seven, three, then three, three, three, then five, two, nineteen

never_show: nineteen is too big to be a prime
maths_rules: 27 = 3 x 3 x 3, so the middle row is 3, 3, 3
190 = 2 x 5 x 19 for the bottom row
45 = 3 x 3 x 5 and the middle cell is 3, so the first column has a 3 and a 5 above and below; 63 = 3 x 3 x 7 has no 5, so the 5 is bottom-left and the 3 is top-left
171 = 3 x 3 x 19 and the middle cell is 3, so the right column has a 3 and a 19; 63 has no 19, so the 19 is bottom-right and the 3 is top-right
42 = 2 x 3 x 7 and the middle cell is 3, so the middle column has a 2 and a 7; the bottom row already has 5 and 19, so the 2 is bottom-middle and the 7 is top-middle
19 is a prime: 2, 3, 4, 5 and every number up to 18 leave a remainder on dividing 19
video_script.design: One idea: fill the forced row first, then place each remaining prime where its row and its column both allow it. Assumes the rules of the puzzle and prime factors. Wrong idea: a big number cannot be a prime. The grid stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is one more puzzle from your book.
<bookmark mark='grid'/>Fill the three by three grid with prime numbers only.
<bookmark mark='right'/>The rows must multiply to sixty three, twenty seven and one hundred and ninety.
<bookmark mark='below'/>The columns must multiply to forty five, forty two and one hundred and seventy one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What goes in the nine cells?

<bookmark mark='break'/>Breaking a product into primes tells us which numbers it needs.

narration: <bookmark mark='mid'/>Step one, start with the row that multiplies to twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Twenty seven is three times three times three, so the middle row is all threes.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, bottom row 190 = 2 x 5 x 19; first column 45 = 3 x 3 x 5 has a 3 in the middle, so 3 and 5 are left; 63 has no 5, so 5 is bottom-left and 3 is top-left

marks.col: 45 = 3 x 3 x 5 is written under the first column

narration: <bookmark mark='bottom'/>Step two, the bottom row multiplies to one hundred and ninety, which is two times five times nineteen.
<bookmark mark='col'/>The first column multiplies to forty five, which is three times three times five.
A three is in the middle, so a three and a five are left.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The top row, sixty three, has no five, so the five goes at the bottom left.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, right column 171 = 3 x 3 x 19 has a 3 in the middle, so 3 and 19 are left; 63 has no 19, so 19 is bottom-right and 3 is top-right

marks.nineteen: 19 goes in the bottom-right cell and 3 in the top-right cell

narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>Step three, look at the right column.
One hundred and seventy one is three times three times nineteen.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The middle is three, so a three and a nineteen are left.
<bookmark mark='nineteen'/>The top row has no nineteen, so the nineteen goes at the bottom right.

narration: <bookmark mark='mid'/>Step four, the middle column multiplies to forty two, which is two times three times seven.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The bottom row has a five and a nineteen, so its middle cell is two. That leaves seven on top.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check the top row. Three times seven times three is sixty three.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks nineteen is too big to be a prime.
<bookmark mark='big'/>It is bigger than every other number in the grid.
<bookmark mark='try'/>But try two, three, four, five, and on up to eighteen, and each one leaves something over.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Only one and nineteen divide it, so nineteen is a prime.
